fatal_errors: The proposed AlCoCrFeNiTi0.5 powder-metallurgy alloy is not the as-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic HEA evaluated in the target study.
The proposed 800–900 °C air or NaCl test is fundamentally different from immersed tribo-corrosion in deionized water at 25–100 °C.

The claimed improvement at the highest temperatures conflicts with the target result, in which wear was minimized near 50 °C and increased at 100 °C because the oxide/tribo-layer repeatedly fractured and was removed.
No equivalent DS2205 comparator or identically conditioned structural-alloy baseline is included.
The sole citation concerns compression and deformation of SLM CoCrFeMnNi, not tribo-corrosion, AlCoCrFeNiTi0.5, spinel-film formation, or the proposed processing route.
explanation: The hypothesis broadly addresses temperature-dependent tribological degradation of an HEA and proposes a testable oxide-mediated mechanism, but it does not reconstruct the target material, intervention, environment, comparator, or observed non-monotonic temperature response. Its spinel-film explanation is plausible in some high-temperature tribo-oxidation systems, yet it is unsupported here and partially opposes the target mechanism, where high temperature destabilizes the tribo-layer rather than producing progressively better protection. The falsification experiment is reasonably discriminating because it measures wear, friction, and oxide formation across temperature, although the environment is left ambiguous and corrosion measurements are optional. Overall, this is an unevidenced alternative rather than a supported reconstruction.
